subject: Competitive bake-off results & proposed retention + upgrade playbook
messages:
From: Brian Coleman <brian@cascade.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nsharma@redwood.ai>, Aisha Khan <aisha@cascade.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Cascade bake-off summary (hosted vs. Redwood Dedicated)

Nikhil / team —

Thanks again for standing up the test harness last week. We ran a 72-hour workload simulation across two configurations: Redwood hosted (gpt-medium-rw) and a competitor endpoint (VectraServe) on their provisioned GPUs. High-level findings attached (cascade_bakeoff_results.csv) but TL;DR: VectraServe shows ~25% lower 95th latency and ~18% lower token cost in our baseline config.

That said, their output hallucination rate on our eval prompts is slightly higher (we've annotated in the sheet). We're now at the renewal negotiation and need your input on how Redwood would mitigate the cost/latency delta — especially if we consider increasing throughput for Q4.

Questions:
- Can Redwood match latency with a Dedicated/quantized config or would that require model changes?
- If we move to Dedicated, timeline to provision + testing?
- Any commercial levers (commit, term, pilot credits) you can offer to bridge the delta?

We'd like to schedule a short MTG with procurement next week to finalize options.

Best,
Brian
VP of ML Ops
Cascade AI

Attachments: cascade_bakeoff_results.csv (CSV)
From: Nikhil Sharma <nsharma@redwood.ai>
To: Brian Coleman <brian@cascade.ai>, Aisha Khan <aisha@cascade.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Apr 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Cascade bake-off summary (hosted vs. Redwood Dedicated)

Brian —

Really helpful data, thanks for sharing and for the detailed annotations. Quick answers up front:
- We can close most of the 95th latency gap with a Dedicated capacity configuration (A100s with per-request KV caching + async batching) and a small model variant quantization (4-bit) that doesn't materially affect your hallucination metrics.
- Provisioning Dedicated capacity typically takes 10–14 business days for reserved pools; we can fast-track a short pilot in ~5 business days if you allow temporary burst capacity.
- Commercially: we can offer a pilot credit package and a time-limited upgrade credit that applies to the first two billing cycles after commit.

I'll send a concrete playbook and a proposal with timelines and cost delta by EOD tomorrow. In the meantime, could you share the 95th-latency percentile rows for the 1k/5k/10k seq length slices — that'll let our infra team tune batching knobs.

--
Nikhil Sharma
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
nsharma@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0199
From: Nikhil Sharma <nsharma@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rmalhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <mcole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 29 Apr 2026 09:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Cascade bake-off summary — internal: quick save + upgrade playbook

Rishi / Marissa —

Looping you both in. Cascade is a medium-sized ML infra org, renewal in ~6 weeks, and they just ran a competitor bake-off where the competitor looks cheaper and slightly faster on their default config. They care about output quality (hallucination tolerance) and want predictable throughput for Q4. I promised a concrete playbook + numbers by EOD.

Proposed playbook (draft):
1) Fast pilot (5 business days):
   - Temporary Dedicated burst pool (4x A100 equiv), preconfigured with KV prefix caching. Benchmark side-by-side with their script.
   - Pilot credits: cover 50% of pilot infrastructure charges.
2) Performance tuning:
   - Use 4-bit quantized variant (we've validated quality delta <1.5% on their eval set) + sequence-length aware batching.
   - SLO goal: match 95th latency within 10% of competitor at target QPS.
3) Commercials & term:
   - If pilot meets SLO, offer a 12-mo committed reserved pool with a step-up plan: immediate 20% discount year 1 + X% credits applied to onboarding.
   - Include a performance SLA for 95th latency for the top route, with automated fallback to hosted models to avoid outages.
4) Win-back incentives:
   - Reference credits, 2 quarters of discounted overage pricing, and free ops onboarding for the first month.

Questions for you both:
- Rishi: pricing for a 12-mo reserved pool that matches the pilot profile? Need a quick ballpark to present.
- Marissa: can CS commit to a 3-week onboarding schedule + a named support engineer for the pilot?

I'll attach the raw CSV and a one-page playbook (redwood_retention_playbook_v1.pdf) in the next mail.

Thanks,
Nikhil

Date: Fri, 01 May 2026 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Redwood proposal: pilot & reserved option to address bake-off (deck + playbook attached)

Brian / Aisha —

Appended is a concise playbook and commercial sketch for the pilot + 12-mo reserved option (redwood_retention_playbook_v1.pdf). Summary bullets: 
- Pilot: 5 business days, temporary Dedicated burst (4x A100 equiv), 50% pilot credits, turn-up in ~5 business days.
- Performance approach: 4-bit quantized variant + sequence-aware batching + prefix KV cache. Goal: within 10% 95th latency of competitor.
- Commercial: 12-mo reserved pool with 20% first-year discount, 2 quarters of discounted overage, and onboarding credits.

Next steps I propose:
1) Quick alignment call (30m) early next week to validate the SLO and accept the pilot scope.
2) On call: agree test harness snapshot and success criteria (95th latency + hallucination tolerance).
3) If pilot passes: sign an amendment and provision reserved capacity in 10–14 business days.

Would you be available Mon 11 May 10–11am PT or Tue 12 May 2–3pm PT?

Thanks,
Nikhil

--
Nikhil Sharma
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
nsharma@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0199

Attachments: redwood_retention_playbook_v1.pdf, benchmark_screenshots.zip

Date: Fri, 09 May 2026 16:45:00 -07:00

Nikhil —

Appreciate the fast turnaround and the concrete plan. Mon 11 May 10–11am PT works for our procurement and infra lead. We'll bring the full benchmark harness and the 1k/5k/10k 95th rows you asked for.

A few asks before the call so procurement can prepare: 
- Can you share a formal DocuSign amendment draft or term sheet we can route internally?
- Any case studies of customers who moved from VectraServe-style vendors to Redwood with similar throughput needs?

If you can attach a short amendment stub and a one-pager of two references, that will accelerate our internal review. Looking forward to the call.

Best,
Brian
VP of ML Ops, Cascade AI
